claim: The HELIX study includes 823 children of European ancestry from six birth cohorts with available blood DNA methylation and gene expression data.
source: The study includes 823 children of European ancestry from the HELIX project with available blood DNA methylation and gene expression data. These children, enrolled in six cohorts, were aged between 6 and 11 years and the number of males and females was balanced (Table 1).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states the sample size, ancestry, and data availability in the Methods section.

claim: The study identified 39,749 statistically significant autosomal cis eQTMs in children's blood.
source: We identified 39,749 blood autosomal cis eQTMs, representing 21,966 unique CpGs (eCpGs, 5.7% of total CpGs) and 8,886 unique transcript clusters (eGenes, 15.3% of total transcript clusters, equivalent to genes).
evidence: This is a primary finding directly stated in the Results section of the Abstract.

claim: 58.8% of all eQTMs showed an inverse relationship between methylation and expression levels.
source: In 87.9% of these cis eQTMs, the eCpG was located at <250 kb from eGene's TSS; and 58.8% of all eQTMs showed an inverse relationship between the methylation and expression levels.
evidence: This percentage is explicitly stated in the Abstract Results section.

claim: Only around half of the autosomal cis-eQTMs eGenes could be captured through annotation of the eCpG to the closest gene.
source: Only around half of the autosomal cis-eQTMs eGenes could be captured through annotation of the eCpG to the closest gene.
evidence: This finding is explicitly stated in the Abstract Results section.

claim: In 40.4% of the eQTMs, the CpG and the eGene were both associated with at least one genetic variant.
source: In 40.4% of the eQTMs, the CpG and the eGene were both associated with at least one genetic variant.
evidence: This percentage is explicitly stated in the Abstract Results section.

claim: The overlap of autosomal cis eQTMs in children's blood with those described in adults was small (13.8%).
source: The overlap of autosomal cis eQTMs in children's blood with those described in adults was small (13.8%), and age-shared cis eQTMs tended to be proximal to the TSS and enriched for genetic variants.
evidence: This finding is explicitly stated in the Abstract Results section.

claim: The epigenome regulates gene expression in a cell/tissue- and time-specific manner.
source: This is orchestrated by the epigenome, which regulates gene expression in a cell/tissue- and time-specific manner (Cavalli and Heard, 2019; Feinberg, 2018; Lappalainen and Greally, 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by three citations to published literature.

claim: The epigenome is responsible for plasticity and cellular memory in response to environmental perturbations.
source: Besides its central role in regulating embryonic and fetal development, X-chromosome inactivation, genomic imprinting, and silencing of repetitive DNA elements, the epigenome is also responsible for the plasticity and cellular memory in response to environmental perturbations (Cavalli and Heard, 2019; Feinberg, 2018; Lappalainen and Greally, 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by three citations to published literature.

claim: Massive epigenetic alterations were initially described in cancer.
source: Massive epigenetic alterations, caused by somatic mutations, age, injury, or environmental exposures, were initially described in cancer (Feinberg, 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: The EWAS Atlas includes 0.5 M associations for 498 traits from 1216 studies, including 155 different cells/tissues.
source: The latter includes 0.5 M associations for 498 traits from 1216 studies, including 155 different cells/tissues.
evidence: This statement describes the content of the EWAS Atlas database.

claim: Most EWAS studies do not have transcriptional data to test the effect of DNA methylation on gene expression.
source: Regarding the latter, most studies do not have transcriptional data to test the effect of DNA methylation on gene expression.
evidence: This is a general observation about the state of EWAS research.

claim: A common approach in EWAS is to assume that CpG DNA methylation affects the expression of the closest gene.
source: When these data are not available, a common approach is to assume that CpG DNA methylation affects the expression of the closest gene (Sharp et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement describes a common practice in the field, supported by a citation.

claim: CpG DNA methylation might regulate distant genes or might not regulate any gene at all.
source: Although this approach is easy to implement, it is limited. Indeed, CpG DNA methylation might regulate distant genes or might not regulate any gene at all (Bonder et al., 2017; Lappalainen and Greally, 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by two citations to published literature.

claim: Most EWAS are conducted in whole blood.
source: As most of the EWAS are conducted in whole blood (Felix et al., 2018; Li et al., 2019), there is a need for comprehensive eQTM studies in this tissue.
evidence: This statement is supported by two citations to published literature.

claim: Available eQTM studies in whole blood only cover samples from adults.
source: To date, available eQTM studies in whole blood only cover samples from adults (Bonder et al., 2017; Kennedy et al., 2018) and their validity in children has not been assessed.
evidence: This statement is supported by two citations and identifies a research gap.

claim: DNA methylation was assessed with the Infinium HumanMethylation450K BeadChip.
source: DNA methylation was assessed with the Infinium HumanMethylation450K BeadChip (Illumina), following manufacturer's protocol at the National Spanish Genotyping Centre (CEGEN), Spain.
evidence: This is a methodological detail explicitly stated in the Methods section.

claim: Gene expression was assessed with the Human Transcriptome Array 2.0 ST arrays.
source: Gene expression, including coding and non-coding transcripts, was assessed with the Human Transcriptome Array 2.0 ST arrays (HTA 2.0) (Affymetrix) at the University of Santiago de Compostela (USC), Spain.
evidence: This is a methodological detail explicitly stated in the Methods section.

claim: Blood cell type proportions were estimated using the Houseman algorithm and the Reinius reference panel.
source: Main blood cell type proportions (CD4+ and CD8+ T cells, natural killer cells, monocytes, eosinophils, neutrophils, and B-cells) were estimated using the Houseman algorithm (Houseman et al., 2012) and the Reinius reference panel (Reinius et al., 2012) from raw methylation data.
evidence: This is a methodological detail explicitly stated in the Methods section, supported by citations.

claim: Each CpG was paired to a median of 30 genes in the analysis.
source: In total, we obtained 13.6 M CpG-Gene pairs, where each CpG was paired to a median of 30 enes; and each ene was paired to a median of 162 CpGs (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This statistic is stated in the text and supported by Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Each gene was paired to a median of 162 CpGs in the analysis.
source: In total, we obtained 13.6 M CpG-Gene pairs, where each CpG was paired to a median of 30 enes; and each ene was paired to a median of 162 CpGs (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This statistic is stated in the text and supported by Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The identified eQTMs comprised 21,966 unique CpGs (5.7% of total CpGs).
source: These eQTMs comprised 21,966 unique CpGs (5.7% of total CpGs) and 8,886 unique enes (15.3% of total enes), of which 6288 were annotated as coding genes.
evidence: This is a primary finding explicitly stated in the Results section.

claim: The identified eQTMs comprised 8,886 unique genes (15.3% of total genes), of which 6288 were annotated as coding genes.
source: These eQTMs comprised 21,966 unique CpGs (5.7% of total CpGs) and 8,886 unique enes (15.3% of total enes), of which 6288 were annotated as coding genes.
evidence: This is a primary finding explicitly stated in the Results section.

claim: 23,355 eQTMs (58.8% of total) showed inverse associations between DNA methylation and gene expression.
source: 23,355 eQTMs (58.8% of total) showed inverse associations, meaning that higher DNA methylation was associated with lower gene expression.
evidence: This is a primary finding explicitly stated in the Results section.

claim: Each eGene was associated with a median of 2 eCpGs.
source: In eQTMs, each eGene was associated with a median of 2 eCpGs, while each eCpG was associated with a median of 1 eGene (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This statistic is stated in the text and supported by Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Each eCpG was associated with a median of 1 eGene.
source: In eQTMs, each eGene was associated with a median of 2 eCpGs, while each eCpG was associated with a median of 1 eGene (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This statistic is stated in the text and supported by Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: eCpGs presented higher methylation variability in the population compared to non-eCpGs.
source: eCpGs presented higher methylation variability in the population (Figure 1—figure supplement 3), and had higher intraclass correlation coefficients, a proxy of low technical error (Sugden et al., 2020; Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: eCpGs had higher intraclass correlation coefficients, indicating lower technical error.
source: eCpGs presented higher methylation variability in the population (Figure 1—figure supplement 3), and had higher intraclass correlation coefficients, a proxy of low technical error (Sugden et al., 2020; Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text, supported by a citation and Figure 1—figure supplement 4.

claim: 13,278 eCpGs (60.4% of total) were measured with probes which had an intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) > 0.4.
source: Indeed, 13,278 eCpGs (60.4% of total) were measured with probes which had an intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) > 0.4, which is indicative of reliable measurements.
evidence: This statistic is explicitly stated in the Results section.

claim: eGenes had higher call rates compared to non-eGenes.
source: Moreover, eGenes had higher call rates (Figure 1—figure supplement 5).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by Figure 1—figure supplement 5.

claim: 87.9% of all eQTMs had the eCpG located at <250 kb from the eGene's TSS.
source: eCpGs tended to be close to the TSS of the targeted eGenes, being this distance <250 Kb for 87.9% of all eQTMs (Figure 2A).
evidence: This percentage is stated in the text and supported by Figure 2A.

claim: The median distance between an eCpG and the TSS of its associated eGene was 1.1 kb (IQR = –33 kb; 65 kb).
source: Globally, the median distance between an eCpG and the TSS of its associated eGene was 1.1 kb (IQR = –33 kb; 65 kb), being eCpGs closer to the TSS in inverse eQTMs than in positive.
evidence: This statistic is explicitly stated in the Results section.

claim: eCpGs were closer to the TSS in inverse eQTMs than in positive eQTMs.
source: Globally, the median distance between an eCpG and the TSS of its associated eGene was 1.1 kb (IQR = –33 kb; 65 kb), being eCpGs closer to the TSS in inverse eQTMs than in positive.
evidence: This comparison is explicitly stated in the Results section.

claim: The median effect size of eQTMs was 0.12 log2 fold change per 0.1 points increase in methylation.
source: In absolute terms, the median effect size was 0.12, being the minimum 0.002 and the maximum 16.0, with 96.3% of the eQTMs with an effect size < 0.5.
evidence: This statistic is explicitly stated in the Results section.

claim: 96.3% of the eQTMs had an effect size < 0.5.
source: In absolute terms, the median effect size was 0.12, being the minimum 0.002 and the maximum 16.0, with 96.3% of the eQTMs with an effect size < 0.5.
evidence: This percentage is explicitly stated in the Results section.

claim: There was an inverse linear association between the eCpG-eGene's TSS distance and the effect size (p-value = 7.75e-9).
source: We observed an inverse linear association between the eCpG-eGene's TSS distance and the effect size (p-value = 7.75e-9, Figure 2B); while we did not observe significant differences in effect size due to the relative orientation of the eCpG (upstream or downstream) with respect to the eGene's TSS (p-value = 0.68).
evidence: This statistical finding is stated in the text and supported by Figure 2B.

claim: There were no significant differences in effect size due to the relative orientation of the eCpG with respect to the eGene's TSS (p-value = 0.68).
source: We observed an inverse linear association between the eCpG-eGene's TSS distance and the effect size (p-value = 7.75e-9, Figure 2B); while we did not observe significant differences in effect size due to the relative orientation of the eCpG (upstream or downstream) with respect to the eGene's TSS (p-value = 0.68).
evidence: This statistical finding is explicitly stated in the Results section.

claim: Mono inverse eCpGs were the most abundant type (36.8%).
source: Mono inverse eCpGs were the most abundant type (36.8%) (Table 2).
evidence: This percentage is stated in the text and supported by Table 2.

claim: CpG-Gene pairs where CpG and Gene were annotated to the same Gene Symbol were more likely eQTMs than CpG-Gene pairs annotated to different Gene Symbols (OR = 11.90, p-value < 2e-16).
source: First, we observed that CpG-Gene pairs where CpG and Gene were annotated to the same Gene Symbol were more likely eQTMs than CpG-Gene pairs annotated to different Gene Symbols or without gene annotation (OR = 11.90, p-value < 2e-16).
evidence: This statistical finding is explicitly stated in the Results section.

claim: In 52.8% of eCpGs with comparable gene annotation, the eCpG was associated with the expression of an eGene coincident with at least one of the Gene Symbols the eCpG was annotated to.
source: In 7,808 out of these 14,797 eCpGs, the eCpG was associated with the expression of an eGene which was coincident with at least one of the Gene Symbols the eCpG was annotated to (52.8% of eCpGs with comparable gene annotation, 35.5% of all eCpGs).
evidence: This percentage is explicitly stated in the Results section.

claim: eCpGs were enriched for CpGs in 5'UTRs and gene body positions.
source: Within this subset, eCpGs were enriched for CpGs in 5'UTRs and gene body positions, while depleted for CpGs in proximal promoters and 3'UTRs (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: eCpGs were depleted for CpGs in proximal promoters and 3'UTRs.
source: Within this subset, eCpGs were enriched for CpGs in 5'UTRs and gene body positions, while depleted for CpGs in proximal promoters and 3'UTRs (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Inverse eCpGs were enriched for CpGs in distal promoters (TSS1500) and 5'UTRs.
source: Interestingly, we observed that inverse and positive eCpGs were enriched for CpGs located in different gene regions: inverse for CpGs in distal promoters (TSS1500) and 5'UTRs; positive for CpGs in gene bodies.
evidence: This finding is explicitly stated in the Results section.

claim: Positive eCpGs were enriched for CpGs in gene bodies.
source: Interestingly, we observed that inverse and positive eCpGs were enriched for CpGs located in different gene regions: inverse for CpGs in distal promoters (TSS1500) and 5'UTRs; positive for CpGs in gene bodies.
evidence: This finding is explicitly stated in the Results section.

claim: eCpGs were depleted for CpG islands.
source: First, we found that eCpGs were depleted for CpG islands, while mostly enriched for CpG island shores, but also for shelves and open sea (Figure 3A).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by Figure 3A.

claim: eCpGs were enriched for CpG island shores, shelves, and open sea.
source: First, we found that eCpGs were depleted for CpG islands, while mostly enriched for CpG island shores, but also for shelves and open sea (Figure 3A).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by Figure 3A.

claim: eCpGs were enriched for several active chromatin states, such as enhancers or active transcription regions.
source: eCpGs were enriched for several active states, such as enhancers or active transcription regions.
evidence: This finding is explicitly stated in the Results section.

claim: Only inverse eCpGs were enriched for proximal promoter states.
source: Nonetheless, we observed some discrepancies between eCpGs subtypes: only inverse eCpGs were enriched for proximal promoter states while only positive eCpGs were depleted for transcription at 5' and 3' (TxFlnk).
evidence: This finding is explicitly stated in the Results section.

claim: Only positive eCpGs were depleted for transcription at 5' and 3' (TxFlnk).
source: Nonetheless, we observed some discrepancies between eCpGs subtypes: only inverse eCpGs were enriched for proximal promoter states while only positive eCpGs were depleted for transcription at 5' and 3' (TxFlnk).
evidence: This finding is explicitly stated in the Results section.

claim: Both positive and inverse eCpGs were enriched for bivalent regulatory states (BivReg).
source: In inactive chromatin states, both positive and inverse eCpGs were enriched for bivalent regulatory states (BivReg), while only positive eCpGs were enriched for repressed and weak repressed Polycomb regions (ReprPC, ReprPCWk) and quiescent regions (Quies).
evidence: This finding is explicitly stated in the Results section.

claim: Only positive eCpGs were enriched for repressed and weak repressed Polycomb regions (ReprPC, ReprPCWk) and quiescent regions (Quies).
source: In inactive chromatin states, both positive and inverse eCpGs were enriched for bivalent regulatory states (BivReg), while only positive eCpGs were enriched for repressed and weak repressed Polycomb regions (ReprPC, ReprPCWk) and quiescent regions (Quies).
evidence: This finding is explicitly stated in the Results section.

claim: eCpGs were enriched for CpGs with medium (> 0.3–0.7) methylation levels and depleted for CpGs with low (0–0.3) or high (> 0.7–1) methylation levels.
source: We found that eCpGs were enriched for CpGs with medium ( > 0.3–0.7) methylation levels and depleted for CpGs with low (0–0.3) or high ( > 0.7–1) methylation levels (Figure 3C).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by Figure 3C.

claim: 5503 out of the 8886 unique Gene Symbols annotated to eGenes were present in Gene Ontology - Biological Processes (GO-BP), leading to 52 enriched terms (q-value < 0.001).
source: 5503 out of the 8886 unique Gene Symbols annotated to eGenes were present in Gene Ontology - Biological Processes (GO-BP), leading to 52 enriched terms (q-value < 0.001) (Supplementary file 1A).
evidence: This finding is explicitly stated in the Results section.

claim: 50% of the enriched GO-BP terms were related to immune responses.
source: As expected from the tissue analyzed, 50% of the terms were related to immune responses (N = 26), followed by terms associated with cellular (N = 16) and metabolic (N = 10) processes.
evidence: This percentage is explicitly stated in the Results section.

claim: eCpGs were enriched for CpGs previously related to phenotypic traits and/or environmental exposures in the EWAS Atlas and EWAS catalog.
source: We found that eCpGs were enriched for CpGs in these EWAS databases in comparison to non eCpGs.
evidence: This finding is explicitly stated in the Results section.

claim: eCpGs had higher total additive heritability than non eCpGs (median difference of 0.31, p-value < 2e-16).
source: First, we found that eCpGs had higher total additive and SNP heritabilities than non eCpGs (median difference of 0.31 and 0.11, respectively, p-value < 2e-16 for both).
evidence: This statistical finding is explicitly stated in the Results section.

claim: eCpGs had higher SNP heritability than non eCpGs (median difference of 0.11, p-value < 2e-16).
source: First, we found that eCpGs had higher total additive and SNP heritabilities than non eCpGs (median difference of 0.31 and 0.11, respectively, p-value < 2e-16 for both).
evidence: This statistical finding is explicitly stated in the Results section.

claim: Total additive and SNP heritabilities were higher for eCpGs associated with a larger number of eGenes.
source: Moreover, total additive and SNP heritabilities were higher for eCpGs associated with a larger number of eGenes (increase of 0.025 and 0.026 points per eGene, respectively, with a p-value < 2e-16 for both) (Figure 4A and B).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by Figure 4A and B.

claim: 10,187 eCpGs (27.8% total eCpGs) presented at least one meQTL.
source: 10,187 eCpGs (27.8% total eCpGs) presented at least one meQTL, being eCpGs enriched in CpGs associated with genetic variants (OR: 11.06, p-value < 2e-6).
evidence: This statistic is explicitly stated in the Results section.

claim: eCpGs were enriched in CpGs associated with genetic variants (OR: 11.06, p-value < 2e-6).
source: 10,187 eCpGs (27.8% total eCpGs) presented at least one meQTL, being eCpGs enriched in CpGs associated with genetic variants (OR: 11.06, p-value < 2e-6).
evidence: This statistical finding is explicitly stated in the Results section.

claim: Among CpGs with meQTLs, eCpGs were associated with a higher number of meQTLs (median: 74, IQR: 27; 162) than non eCpGs (median: 32, IQR = 10; 77).
source: In addition, among CpGs with meQTLs, eCpGs were associated with a higher number of meQTLs (median: 74, IQR: 27; 162) than non eCpGs (median: 32, IQR = 10; 77).
evidence: This comparison is explicitly stated in the Results section.

claim: The study identified 1,368,613 SNP-CpG-Gene trios with consistent direction of effect.
source: After multiple-testing correction, we identified 1,368,613 SNP-CpG-Gene trios with consistent direction of effect, and 12,799 with inconsistent direction.
evidence: This finding is explicitly stated in the Results section.

claim: The SNP-CpG-Gene trios comprised 16,055 unique eQTMs (40.4% of significant eQTMs).
source: These formers comprised 16,055 unique eQTMs (40.4% of significant eQTMs); 8503 unique eCpGs (38.7% of total eCpGs); and 4098 unique eGenes (46.1% of total eGenes), of which 3154 were coding (50.2% of total coding eGenes).
evidence: This statistic is explicitly stated in the Results section.

claim: The SNP-CpG-Gene trios comprised 8503 unique eCpGs (38.7% of total eCpGs).
source: These formers comprised 16,055 unique eQTMs (40.4% of significant eQTMs); 8503 unique eCpGs (38.7% of total eCpGs); and 4098 unique eGenes (46.1% of total eGenes), of which 3154 were coding (50.2% of total coding eGenes).
evidence: This statistic is explicitly stated in the Results section.

claim: The SNP-CpG-Gene trios comprised 4098 unique eGenes (46.1% of total eGenes), of which 3154 were coding (50.2% of total coding eGenes).
source: These formers comprised 16,055 unique eQTMs (40.4% of significant eQTMs); 8503 unique eCpGs (38.7% of total eCpGs); and 4098 unique eGenes (46.1% of total eGenes), of which 3154 were coding (50.2% of total coding eGenes).
evidence: This statistic is explicitly stated in the Results section.

claim: eQTMs were enriched for CpGs whose methylation change from birth to childhood/adolescence according to the MeDALL and Epidelta projects.
source: We found that eCpGs were enriched for CpGs whose methylation change in both MeDALL and Epidelta databases, but more markedly for CpGs reported in MeDALL (Figure 5A).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by Figure 5A.

claim: Positive and inverse eCpGs showed stronger ORs for CpGs with increased and decreased methylation levels over age, respectively.
source: In both databases, positive and inverse eCpGs showed stronger ORs for CpGs with increased and decreased methylation levels over age, respectively.
evidence: This finding is explicitly stated in the Results section.

claim: 57.9% of eQTMs with p-value < 1e-5 in GTP were also eQTMs in HELIX.
source: We observed that 57.9% and 35.3% of eQTMs with p-value < 1e-5 in GTP and MESA were also eQTMs in HELIX, thus age-shared eQTMs (Figure 5B).
evidence: This percentage is stated in the text and supported by Figure 5B.

claim: 35.3% of eQTMs with p-value < 1e-5 in MESA were also eQTMs in HELIX.
source: We observed that 57.9% and 35.3% of eQTMs with p-value < 1e-5 in GTP and MESA were also eQTMs in HELIX, thus age-shared eQTMs (Figure 5B).
evidence: This percentage is stated in the text and supported by Figure 5B.

claim: More than 90% of age-shared eQTMs have the same direction in GTP/MESA than in HELIX.
source: More than 90% of age-shared eQTMs have the same direction in GTP/MESA than in HELIX (Supplementary file 1D).
evidence: This percentage is explicitly stated in the Results section.

claim: Only 5471 (13.8%) of the eQTMs identified in HELIX children were reported in adult GTP or MESA catalogues at p-value < 1e-5.
source: Only 5471 (13.8%) of the eQTMs identified in HELIX children were reported in adult GTP or MESA catalogues at p-value < 1e-5 (Figure 5C).
evidence: This percentage is stated in the text and supported by Figure 5C.

claim: Age-shared eQTMs involved 4364 eCpGs and 1689 eGenes.
source: Age-shared eQTMs involved 4364 eCpGs and 1689 eGenes, whereas children-specific eQTMs involved 19,584 eCpGs and 8429 eGenes.
evidence: This statistic is explicitly stated in the Results section.

claim: Children-specific eQTMs involved 19,584 eCpGs and 8429 eGenes.
source: Age-shared eQTMs involved 4364 eCpGs and 1689 eGenes, whereas children-specific eQTMs involved 19,584 eCpGs and 8429 eGenes.
evidence: This statistic is explicitly stated in the Results section.

claim: Age-shared eCpGs had higher reliability (higher ICC) than child-specific eCpGs.
source: Age-shared eCpGs had higher reliability (higher ICC) (Figure 5—figure supplement 2) and tended to be closer to the TSS than child-specific eCpGs (Figure 5—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: Age-shared eCpGs tended to be closer to the TSS than child-specific eCpGs.
source: Age-shared eCpGs had higher reliability (higher ICC) (Figure 5—figure supplement 2) and tended to be closer to the TSS than child-specific eCpGs (Figure 5—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by Figure 5—figure supplement 3.

claim: Age-shared eCpGs showed higher ORs of enrichment for meQTLs (OR = 20.7) than child-specific eCpGs (OR = 10.3).
source: Both types of eCpGs were enriched for meQTLs compared to non eCpGs, with the OR being stronger for age-shared eCpGs (OR = 20.7) than for child-specific eCpGs (OR = 10.3).
evidence: This comparison is explicitly stated in the Results section.

claim: The catalogue of eQTMs is publicly available at https://helixomics.isglobal.org/ and at Dryad (doi:10.5061/dryad.fxpnvx0t0).
source: The complete catalogue of eQTMs can be downloaded from https://helixomics.isglobal.org/ and from Dryad (doi:10.5061/dryad.fxpnvx0t0).
evidence: This information is explicitly stated in the Results section.

claim: The causal relationship between DNA methylation and gene expression cannot be definitely inferred from this study.
source: We want to point out that the causal relationship between DNA methylation and gene expression cannot be definitely inferred from our study.
evidence: This is a limitation explicitly acknowledged by the authors.

claim: There is evidence suggesting that DNA methylation could be a consequence of gene expression, as opposed to the often assumed concept that regulation of gene expression is mediated by DNA methylation.
source: Indeed, there is some evidence suggesting that DNA methylation could be a consequence of gene expression, as opposed to the often assumed concept that regulation of gene expression is mediated by DNA methylation (Gutierrez-Arcelus et al., 2013; Jones, 2012; Kim et al., 2020).
evidence: This statement is supported by three citations to published literature.

claim: The influence of environmental factors is more relevant for immune pathways, while genetic factors might be more determinant in regulating metabolic processes in blood cells.
source: Interestingly, the number of GO-BP terms related to immune and cellular functions was reduced for eGenes under genetic control, in comparison to all eGenes; on the contrary, the number of GO-BP terms involving metabolic processes was maintained. This may suggest that the influence of environmental factors is more relevant for immune pathways, while genetic factors might be more determinant in regulating metabolic processes in blood cells.
evidence: This is an interpretation inferred from the GO-BP enrichment results.

claim: The small overlap between adult and child eQTMs has different explanations: methodological issues, statistical methods and power, cohort-specific environmental exposures, and cellular composition.
source: This small overlap between adult and child eQTMs has different explanations: methodological issues, such as gene expression platforms with low overlap; statistical methods and statistical power; cohort-specific environmental exposures; and cellular composition.
evidence: The authors explicitly list potential explanations for the observed overlap.

claim: DNA methylation and gene expression change with age.
source: Despite the effect of these methodological and confounding factors, it is known that DNA methylation and gene expression change with age (Melé et al., 2015; Mulder et al., 2021; Xu et al., 2017); consequently, we could expect only partial overlap between adult and child eQTMs.
evidence: This statement is supported by three citations to published literature.

claim: Age-shared eCpGs represent eQTMs that are persistent over time or are easier to detect due to stronger effects.
source: The short list of age-shared eCpGs tended to encompass CpGs located in promoters and regulated by genetic variants. Moreover, the overall location of eQTMs in regulatory elements was similar between adults and children (Gutierrez-Arcelus et al., 2015; Küpers et al., 2019). This could represent a specific characteristic of eQTMs that are persistent over time. An alternative explanation is that this kind of eQTMs (genetically regulated and close to the TSS) are easier to be detected and shared among any two studies because they show stronger effects.
evidence: The authors provide two possible interpretations of the age-shared eCpG characteristics.

claim: CpG probes have different measurement error and thus different reliability and reproducibility.
source: As previously described (Sugden et al., 2020), CpG probes have different measurement error and thus different reliability and reproducibility.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: CpGs measured with less error have more chances of being found associated with traits and thus reported in EWAS catalogues.
source: As previously described (Sugden et al., 2020), CpG probes have different measurement error and thus different reliability and reproducibility. Consequently, CpGs measured with less error have more chances of being found associated with traits and thus reported in EWAS catalogues.
evidence: This is a logical inference from the statement about measurement error.

claim: CpG probe reliability is dependent on DNA methylation level and variance.
source: In this line, enrichments of eCpGs for CpGs listed in the EWAS Atlas or in the MeDALL project were markedly attenuated when only considering CpGs measured with good reliability. Moreover, CpG probe reliability is dependent on DNA methylation level and variance (highly unmethylated or highly methylated CpGs, which tend to have low variances, are measured with more error); and genomic regulatory elements are characterized by particular methylation levels.
evidence: This statement is explicitly made in the Discussion section.

claim: The study reports all CpG-gene pairs tested in the analysis, as opposed to existing blood eQTM catalogues which only reported pairs passing a given p-value threshold.
source: First, we report all CpG-gene pairs we tested in our analysis, as opposed to existing blood eQTM catalogues which only reported pairs passing a given p-value threshold (Bonder et al., 2017; Kennedy et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a strength of the study explicitly stated by the authors.

claim: The catalogue only covers a fraction of all CpG-Gene pairs, as both the methylation and gene expression arrays have limited resolution.
source: The catalogue also has some limitations. First, it only covers a fraction of all CpG-Gene pairs, as both the methylation and gene expression arrays have limited resolution.
evidence: This is a limitation explicitly acknowledged by the authors.

claim: The catalogue does not include sex chromosomes.
source: Second, the catalogue does not include sex chromosomes which require more complex analyses to address X-inactivation and sex-specific effects that will be addressed in future studies.
evidence: This is a limitation explicitly acknowledged by the authors.

claim: Due to statistical power limitations, only cis effects were tested.
source: Third, due to statistical power limitations, only cis effects were tested.
evidence: This is a limitation explicitly acknowledged by the authors.

claim: Models were adjusted for blood cell type composition, which might have resulted in over-adjustment in some CpG-Gene pairs.
source: Fifth, models were adjusted for blood cell type composition and, while this has allowed us to control for major differences in methylation and gene expression among blood cell types, it might also have resulted in over-adjustment in some CpG-Gene pairs.
evidence: This is a limitation explicitly acknowledged by the authors.

claim: The analysis of bulk data might have limited the identification of eQTMs specific to a subset of blood cell types.
source: Moreover, the analysis of bulk data might have limited the identification of eQTMs specific to a subset of blood cell types, the identification of which would need more sophisticated statistical and/or experimental methods.
evidence: This is a limitation explicitly acknowledged by the authors.
